syndicate_4747_2024.shared_basis_gap_reason: The control miss is -2,150 (-7.15%), implied below accounts. An ultimate/underwriting basis (unearned premium included) would push implied incurred ABOVE earned incurred, so it cannot explain a shortfall; there is no outside column. Constant balance-sheet-date translation does explain part: 2023 FX on claims outstanding (570) (2023 p30 note 4 'Effect of movements in exchange rates (570)') is about 27% of the 2,150 gap; 1,580 (5.3% of accounts) stays unexplained, so the control is outside 5% even after FX. In year t the same FX item is 3,225 (2024 p35 note 6), 6.4% of the 50,696 miss. The year t miss comes from a different mechanism (paid row at calendar-year level, latest diagonal = reserve + 2024 paid, 2022/2023 end-2023 cells restated by +7.2m/+27.2m vs the 2023 report) that is absent from the 2023 table. So no named difference present in both years explains both
syndicate_4747_2024.contradicts_premises: (1) The control is not within 5% (7.15%); passes only if a shared basis gap is shown, and none can be. (2) The 2024 table's printed paid row is not cumulative to date, so the table's 'cumulative incurred' for mature years is not on one basis across its own columns; the year t table also fails the paid check one-sidedly (21,135 vs 34.6m expected). (3) The 2023 report's end-2023 diagonal (51,304) differs materially from the 2024 report's end-2023 diagonal (85,355): a restatement of 2022-2023 columns, not FX. (4) If instead the measure were reserve movement plus paid, (75,447-38,860)+22,111 = 58,698, +3,225 FX = 61,923 = accounts: the accounts reconcile internally, the table does not.
syndicate_4747_2024.verdict_hint: year t table fails (-81.9%); control misses by 7.15% with no shared basis gap, so it does not tie within 5% and the 10% allowance is not supported

syndicate_780_2016.shared_basis_gap_reason: The only named outside item in both tables is the '2010 & prior' row, which prints a balance at one date and no incurred or payments, so its movement in 2015 and 2016 cannot be read off any page. The miss sign and size are consistent with it: the table (cells only) exceeds accounts by 9.5m in 2015 and 7.7m in 2016, which would need an '& prior' incurred of about -9.5m and -7.7m, both within the accounts' stated gross prior-year releases ((32.2)m in 2015, (15.6)m in 2016, p25 and p27). That is plausible, not shown. Against 'yes': the 2016 table is not on the same basis as the 2015 table (its end-2015 diagonal is 173.6m lower and '& prior' balance is 113.7m higher than the 2015 report's), so a shared '& prior' movement cannot be assumed to be the same kind of gap in the two years. And in any case the 10% clause needs year t miss >= 3x control's: the year t miss is 0.81x control's
syndicate_780_2016.contradicts_premises: (1) The year t miss (+5.56%, 7.7m) is smaller than the control miss (+9.44%, 9.5m): ratio 0.81, so the 'at least three times' condition fails and the control is not within 5% (9.44%). On the pages the control does not tie better than year t does. (2) Year t is only marginally outside 5% (5.56%). (3) The 2016 table restated its own end-2015 cells (528.0 vs 701.6 in the 2015 report) and shifted about 114m of reserves into '2010 & prior'; M read from the 2016 table (u<=2014 latest less 2016's own end-2015 cells: 2011 +2.4, 2012 +4.4, 2013 +3.4, 2014 +14.7 = +24.9) uses restated history. (4) Both reports' accounts do tie to their own balance sheets and to each other (2015 gross paid 116.2 and change 15.5 unchanged in the 2016 report). (5) OCR note: the 2016 note p27 prints current year '164.2'; arithmetic (154.2 - 15.6 = 138.6) shows it is 154.2, an OCR misread, no effect on figures used
syndicate_780_2016.verdict_hint: year t table is within 5.6% of the accounts on incurred (cells only, '& prior' excluded) and its miss is smaller than the control's 9.4%, so the premise of rule 1 (year t fails, control ties) is not met on the pages
